_: Who each model in the IRI plume is. Type (dynamical / statistical) is not written by hand: it comes from the legend of the plume figure itself and is stored with every issue. The description says which centre runs it and what kind of machine it is; where we are not certain of the details we say only what the plume itself states. The performance next to a model on the panel (class, mean error, issues below reality) is measured by us against the official ONI, not taken from the centre.
src: IRI/CCSR ENSO forecast plume, iri.columbia.edu; the model roster and the dynamical/statistical split come from the figure legend of each issue.

kinds.dyn: Dynamical: a coupled ocean–atmosphere model that integrates the physics forward in time. Expensive, and in principle able to produce a state it has never seen.
kinds.stat: Statistical: a model fitted to past data — regression, linear inverse modelling, or a neural network. Cheap and often sharp, but a strong event outside its training range is exactly where it is weakest.
kinds.avg: An average across the plume: combined, dynamical only, or statistical only. Not a model of its own.

AUS-ACCESS.note: The ACCESS-S coupled seasonal system, the model behind the Australian ENSO outlook.

BCC DIAP.note: A coupled seasonal prediction system run by the Chinese national climate centre.

BCC_RZDM.note: A statistical companion to the same centre's dynamical system.

CMC CANSIP.note: CanSIPS, the Canadian seasonal prediction system, a multi-model ensemble of Canadian coupled models.

CMCC SPS4.note: The Euro-Mediterranean Centre's seasonal prediction system, version 4.

COLA CCSM4.note: A seasonal configuration of the CCSM4 climate model.

CPC MRKOV.note: A Markov model: a statistical scheme that propagates the present ocean state forward with transitions fitted to history. One of the oldest members of the plume.

CS-IRI-MM.note: A multi-model ensemble assembled at IRI itself.

CSU CLIPR.note: A statistical scheme built on climate predictors.

IAP-NN.org: Institute of Atmospheric Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences
IAP-NN.note: A neural network trained on past ENSO evolution.

IOCAS ICM.org: Institute of Oceanology, Chinese Academy of Sciences
IOCAS ICM.note: An intermediate coupled model: simpler physics than a full climate model, tuned for the tropical Pacific.

JAMSTEC CNN.note: A convolutional neural network trained on maps of ocean state.

JMA.note: The Japanese operational coupled seasonal system.

KMA.note: The Korean operational coupled seasonal system.

LDEO.org: Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory, Columbia University, USA
LDEO.note: The Zebiak–Cane lineage: the intermediate coupled model that made the first successful ENSO forecasts in the 1980s.

MetFRANCE.note: The French operational coupled seasonal system.

NASA GMAOv3.org: NASA Global Modeling and Assimilation Office, USA

NTU CODA.note: A statistical scheme using ocean data assimilation output as its predictors.

SINTEX-F.note: A coupled model long used for ENSO and Indian Ocean prediction.

TONGJI-ML.note: A machine-learning model, one of the newer members of the plume.

UCLA-TCD.org: University of California, Los Angeles, USA
UCLA-TCD.note: A statistical scheme in the plume.

UW PSL-LIM.org: University of Washington with NOAA PSL, USA
UW PSL-LIM.note: A linear inverse model: it learns how anomalies evolve on average and propagates them forward.

UW PSL-CSLIM.org: University of Washington with NOAA PSL, USA
UW PSL-CSLIM.note: A cyclostationary linear inverse model, the seasonally varying version of the same idea.

Wyrtki-CSLIM.org: Linear inverse modelling, named for Klaus Wyrtki
Wyrtki-CSLIM.note: A cyclostationary linear inverse model built around the ocean heat recharge that Wyrtki described.

XRO.note: A low-order model of the recharge oscillator kind, extended to other basins.

COMBINED AVG.note: The average of all plume members, dynamical and statistical.

DYN Average.note: The average of the dynamical members only.

STAT Average.note: The average of the statistical members only.
